issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs students to use StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute, but the UML in the same problem statement shows the type as String. This contradicts the specification students should follow and leaves them unclear which type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either update the UML to indicate name: StringBuilder or change the textual instruction to require a String. Prefer updating the UML to name: StringBuilder if the intention is to teach using StringBuilder, and add a note about expected getter/setter signatures.

issues.description: The solution implementation defines Animal.name as a String (private String name;), which conflicts with the problem statement's explicit instruction to use StringBuilder for the name attribute. This cross-artifact mismatch can confuse students and cause tests or grading to expect a different type.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by changing the Animal.name attribute to a StringBuilder and adjust the constructor, getter, and setter accordingly (e.g., private StringBuilder name; public StringBuilder getName(); public void setName(StringBuilder newName);). Alternatively, if String is intended, update the problem statement to remove the StringBuilder requirement.
